en: My name is Maurice.
All my life, I have worked to lay
railway lines in London...
And it paid off: here in London now,
many rails have been laid,
and stations built too.
Compared with the old days, it's quicker and
safer to travel now.
Don't you agree?
And it paid off: rails now run from London
to the provinces, there's an Underground,
and many stations have been built.
Wouldn't you agree?
For all my trips to City Hall,
there's no progress at all.
My venture just isn't going well...
London now has many stations, and rails
have been laid; travel is far easier now.
But...
Through a new endeavour, the railway could
become far, far more useful to us.
That is what I believe...
To make that plan a reality, I've been
coming here to City Hall day after day.
Maurice, what exactly is this idea
of yours?
